title: Understanding SVD
text: The Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of a matrix X is given by X $$=$$ U*S*V**T, where U and V are orthogonal matrices, and S is a diagonal matrix containing the singular values.

title: Relation to Variance
text: The sum of the squares of the singular values (s) is equal to the total variance of the data matrix X. In this case, $$\sum s^2$$ $$=$$ $$121$$.

title: Finding s[1]
text: To find s[1], consider that the singular values are typically ordered from largest to smallest. You need to find the value of s[1] that, when squared and added to the squares of the other singular values, equals $$121$$.
